messages:
Maya Ortiz: FYI prepping options for Evergreen Systems — they want Private with Dedicated rates but no external network egress. want something we can present without a multi-page SOW.
Hannah Lee (Sales): They pushed hard on predictable cost. prefer committed units vs ad-hoc PS invoices. also asked about SLA parity with hosted dedicated.
Raj Patel: Thinking SKU approach: base Private commit (mapped to our Dedicated GPU tiers) + Airgap Compliance SKU with two variants: Lite (per-node ops fee) and Managed (higher flat + PS days). keeps quoting simple.
Nina Brooks (Finance): Lite vs Managed modelling: Lite = lower sticker, higher variable margin risk; Managed = higher upfront but predictable. propose amortizing first-year install engineering into Managed option.
Leo Zhang: Eng constraints: airgap work requires signed offline packages, authenticated installers, and a fallback for webhooks. feature impact: disable streaming callbacks, add polling alternative. effort estimate: Lite = 3 dev sprints + 1 ops sprint; Managed = 5 dev + 2 ops.
Samir Gupta (Legal): Contract notes: "no egress" must be narrowly defined. propose Annex A enumerating allowed endpoints (security scans, CVE feeds, telemetry if opted-in). also require change-control windows for upgrades. will draft template.
Maya Ortiz: Launch criteria for listing the SKU in pricebook: 1) concise runbook (<= 2 pages) for installs + upgrades, 2) pricing cells (commit tiers + node fee + PS day rate), 3) legal annex starter, 4) Console flag to hide/disable outbound integrations.
Hannah Lee (Sales): Also ask for a quick TCO blurb — show 3-year cost comparison: Hosted Dedicated vs Private+Airgap(Lite) vs Private+Airgap(Managed). buyers like simple math.
Raj Patel: I'll build a pricing grid CSV: GPU-commit tiers aligned to Dedicated table, per-node ops ($/node/mo), managed flat surcharge ($/month) and PS day rates. include example discounts for 2- and 3-year commits.
Nina Brooks (Finance): Add finance caveat: revenue recognition differs for PS vs commit. we need Billing to accept separate invoice lines: commit, node-maintenance, one-time install. also recommend minimum 12-month commit for Lite.
Leo Zhang: For Console work: small API & UI changes to toggle public integrations per-customer and surface a "airgap mode" badge. estimate 2 sprints. plus packaging/signing pipeline 2 sprints. total 4 sprints for minimal feature set.
Samir Gupta (Legal): Draft clause (starter):
```
Customer shall operate the Redwood Private runtime within a network environment that does not permit outbound connections to public internet endpoints, except for those endpoints explicitly listed and agreed in Annex A. Redwood will not transmit Customer data to Redwood-controlled services without Customer's prior written consent. Maintenance and upgrade procedures will follow the change-control process in Annex B.
```
I'll add liability caps and maintenance exception language.
ops-bot: Reminder  Upload install checklist to OpsRunbook repo and tag oncall when ready.
Maya Ortiz: OK timeline: if Raj posts grid + Nina signs off on economics + Samir posts redline, Hannah will present both Lite & Managed options in customer meeting Wed. can we hit EOD for artifacts?
Raj Patel: Will upload CSV and a short TCO sheet by 6pm.
Leo Zhang: Will paste the 2-page runbook draft and a minimal Console changelog by 5:30pm.
Nina Brooks (Finance): I'll validate the numbers and comment on acceptable minimums by 5:45pm.
Samir Gupta (Legal): I'll post the annex + quick redline by EOD.
Hannah Lee (Sales): Perfect. if we have two clean options with clear SLA/support tradeoffs we should be able to close. thanks team :rocket:
